title: Amptec bottom CALL steady red | Model-Specific Guide
description: Identify amptec bottom call steady red, distinguish the documented indicator and arrange safe model-specific assessment. Read the matching manufacturer manual.
answer: A steady red bottom CALL is the 100°C control-trip indication in the cited Amptec manual. Do not bypass protection or repeatedly reset.

sections.heading: Meaning and model scope
paragraphs: This is not the same condition as a flashing bottom CALL. Internal sensor mounting and control faults need competent checks. Treat the alarm as a safety-related operating condition, not confirmation that one particular spare part will fix it.

sections.heading: Record the complete pattern
paragraphs: Identify the installed Amptec model and the control-panel layout. Record the light position, colour, whether it flashes and whether the heating demand was active. These guides are based on the cited installation and user manual; they are not a universal map for every Heatrae Sadia appliance.

sections.heading: Safe next step
paragraphs: Do not remove electrical covers, measure live voltage, bypass protective controls or repeatedly reset an alarm. The manufacturer reset sequence requires the fault to be corrected and suitable water and circulation conditions established. That is different from repeatedly cycling power to conceal an unresolved fault.

sections.heading: Discuss the assessment
paragraphs: Call 020 7205 4433 with the label, visible pattern and postcode. Amptec is an electric flow boiler; the business must establish the required electrical and heating competence rather than infer it from a G3 cylinder qualification alone.

faqs.question: Is a steady bottom red CALL the normal heating-demand light?
faqs.answer: No. In the cited Amptec manual it is a control-trip indication; the normal demand indicator is green, not steady red.
